cells.tense: You are moving toward a shared goal and the pull is strong without running you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are driving toward this week, name the single next step, and take it at a pace you can keep past this week.
cells.core:
You take what a group cares about and you move it somewhere concrete — a plan, a room full of people, a thing built. The energy runs high and it does not run you. You steer it. The direction holds through resistance without eating you up, and that is rarer than it sounds.

Because the direction holds, something steadier is available and it is not more motion. It is telling the truth about where this stands, plainly, rough parts included. The momentum is already doing its job. What you can tune is what it is pointed at, and whether you have said yes to that out loud. The next move is yours to call, not the push's.
cells.sheetLine: You are driving what people care about somewhere — steadily.
cells.verb: chasing what people actually share until it becomes something they can carry
cells.place: the stretch where momentum runs between wanting something and having it

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead the shared thing already lands and you are living there before it arrives.
cells.ask: Hold one thing you are pushing toward unshared for a full day and notice what the wait itself tells you.
cells.core:
You are pushing the shared thing hard, and fast, at a pace it did not agree to. Somewhere ahead is the version where it all lands, and you keep working from there — one more push, one more proof it is real. The push is costing you the exact thing you are pushing for.

Here is the bend. You stop letting it develop. You drive it up before anything can come back, because the space between reaching and response opens by itself — that is what the space is for. Your momentum is real and useful; right now it is outrunning its own answer. The part that would steady this is a decision about what the structure can actually hold, and acting from that.

cells.tense: You were headed somewhere with other people once, and you have not moved since.
cells.ask: Write down one goal you dropped and the one reason it dropped; then take a single small step on it, or one clear step toward something its shape fits.
cells.core:
The motion is not gone. It is behind you. You set the destination down — maybe when it ran into walls, maybe when it asked you to be seen — and the body of it has gone quiet.

What is missing is not feeling and not more push, which is why trying harder with the old want does not work. What is missing sits a step back: the picture underneath the target. Look at what the direction was actually for. You can still want the thing and not have a route to it; you can want it small, kept close, without forcing it at anyone. Name the aim before the want wakes up, and let wanting be optional.

cells.tense: You are already moving other people toward something and describing it as simply how the work goes.
cells.ask: State one thing you are already steering — to yourself, in writing — and who it serves, and keep steering while you know it.
cells.core:
You are moving things — bringing people along, keeping the aim pointed — and you call it being useful, or just how it goes. The driving is real. It is shaping what people do, which goals get carried, which quietly get dropped, who hears about it and who does not.

That part is a decision, and it is a smaller, plainer thing than the size of the push makes it feel. Saying it out loud is real work in a direction you already run: you lose a little of the easy line of it, the part that does not need explaining. What is left is narrower and more usable — you know what you are moving and what for, and the direction stays yours.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim in the drafts: that the driving energy is spent specifically on people ('converting', 'borrowed approval') — the record only says energy is channeled toward a destination, so I will keep any relational reading as a possible instance, not the mechanism. A reader could reasonably say it is solo work, not a group, that the momentum runs to; the picture and the mechanism hold either way, and the ask does not require a person to be present. The ask survives a wrong read: it is one real next step either way, and no progress is made conditional on it. The sentence that served me more than the person was 'before it cools' — it was atmosphere, not their life — so it is gone.

The remaining risk is in status 4 — saying someone else's goal is being carried could be overridden by the reader, so I framed it as something they can disown ('you'd call it being useful') rather than a settled fact about them. The asks do not require anyone else to be present and nothing is promised, so they hold even if my read is wrong. The sentence that served me over the person was the 'signing it' figure in status 4 — it looked good and said less than the plain thing — so it is gone.

The remaining risk in status 4 is still that a reader could say they are not steering anyone — the core is framed as an offer they can disown rather than a fact about them, and the ask works whether or not anyone else is involved.
